slides.heading: Reception — Spring 2, Week 1
slides.sub: New sounds taught directly, practised and applied in words, captions and the matching decodable book.

slides.heading: Mon
slides.objective: Learn the new sound "oa" (/əʊ/) and start reading and spelling words that use it.

slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="boat" class="wp-icon wp-raster" data-picture="boat"><image href="data:image/png;base64," x="0" y="0" width="100" height="100" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"/></svg>

slides.mnemonic: Otto the duckling floats along, round and steady, oa-oa, wherever the pond takes him.

character.name: Otto
character.blurb: Otto is a calm little duckling who floats in a slow, steady circle no matter how choppy the pond gets.

slides.pronunciation_note: A long, rounded sound, 'oa' as in 'boat' — round your lips into an O shape and let it glide.
slides.formation_cue: Write 'o', then 'a', close together — two letters, one sound.
slides.action: Round your lips into an O, rock gently side to side like floating, and say oa-oa.
slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="boat" class="wp-icon wp-raster" data-picture="boat"><image href="data:image/png;base64," x="0" y="0" width="100" height="100" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"/></svg>

slides.tip: The 'y' at the end makes the long 'igh' sound instead of a usual 'y' sound — point to something that belongs to you and say 'my' to anchor the meaning.

slides.dictation: Rain can soak a thin coat.

slides.heading: Tue
slides.objective: Learn the new sound "oo" (/uː/) and start reading and spelling words that use it.

slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="moon" class="wp-icon wp-raster" data-picture="moon"><image href="data:image/png;base64," x="0" y="0" width="100" height="100" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"/></svg>

slides.mnemonic: Luna the owl hoots a long, deep call across the moonlit garden, oo-oo.

character.name: Luna
character.blurb: Luna only hoots at night, a long deep oo-oo call that carries right across the garden.

slides.pronunciation_note: A long, deep sound, 'oo' as in 'moon' — round your lips small and hold it, this is the LONG version of oo.
slides.formation_cue: Write 'o' twice, close together — two letters, one sound.
slides.action: Cup your hands around your mouth and hoot a long, low oo-oo.
slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="moon" class="wp-icon wp-raster" data-picture="moon"><image href="data:image/png;base64," x="0" y="0" width="100" height="100" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"/></svg>

slides.heading: Wed
slides.objective: Learn the new sound "oo (short, as in book)" (/ʊ/) and start reading and spelling words that use it.

slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="book" class="wp-icon wp-raster" data-picture="book"><image href="data:image/png;base64," x="0" y="0" width="100" height="100" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"/></svg>

slides.mnemonic: Bobbin the hedgehog gives a quick, soft puff, oo-oo, when he's pushing a heavy pinecone.

character.name: Bobbin
character.blurb: Bobbin is a small, huffing hedgehog who gives short, quick puffs whenever he's pushing something heavy.

slides.pronunciation_note: A short, light sound, 'oo' as in 'book' — quick and soft, this is the SHORT version, different from the long 'oo' in 'moon'. The two 'oo' sounds are easy to mix up: one holds long (moon), this one is quick and clipped (book).
slides.formation_cue: Write 'o' twice, close together, just like the long 'oo' — the letters are exactly the same, only the sound is different.
slides.action: Give a quick, soft puff of breath, oo-oo, like you're pushing something heavy just twice.
slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="book" class="wp-icon wp-raster" data-picture="book"><image href="data:image/png;base64," x="0" y="0" width="100" height="100" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"/></svg>

slides.note: Not enough sounds taught yet to build a whole word — practise oral blending and sound recognition only today.

slides.dictation: A light is on in the room.

slides.heading: Thu
slides.objective: Extra practice blending and segmenting everything taught this week — no new content today.

slides.dictation: A cook can look at a book.

slides.heading: Fri
slides.objective: Revisit everything taught this week, read the matched decodable book, and check how securely it has been learned.
